intro: Calculating freight broker profit margins requires moving beyond simple markups to ensure your business remains solvent. Freight brokerage is a high-competition space where net margins often sit between 3 and 8 percent of gross revenue, making every dollar count.

blocks.text: Why calculating freight broker profit margins is difficult

Many brokers struggle because they confuse markup with margin. A markup is a percentage added to your cost. A margin is the percentage of the total revenue that is profit. If you pay a carrier 900 dollars and charge a shipper 1000 dollars, your margin is 10 percent. If you add a 10 percent markup to the 900 dollar cost, you charge 990 dollars. That small difference adds up over hundreds of loads. It is the primary reason brokers lose money without realizing it.
The danger of booked versus realized margins

The most common mistake is tracking booked margins instead of realized margins. A booked margin is what you expect to make when you sign the load. A realized margin is what you actually keep after fuel surcharges, detention fees, and carrier short pays are settled. If your TMS does not pull data from your accounting software, you are likely looking at incomplete numbers. You need to see the full financial picture in one place to understand your true profitability.

blocks.text: If you are using Excel or Google Sheets, use the formula (Revenue - Cost) / Revenue to calculate your margin percentage. Do not rely on (Revenue - Cost) / Cost, which calculates your markup.
blocks.title: Stop the markup trap

blocks.text: Using your Mac for margin analysis

Most modern brokerage tools run in your browser. Whether you use Chrome, Safari, or Brave, you can access your TMS or accounting platform without needing a Windows machine. If you must use legacy software, tools like Parallels allow you to run Windows apps on your Mac. However, moving to web-based platforms is safer for your data and easier to maintain.

faq.question: What is the difference between markup and margin?
faq.answer: Markup is the percentage added to your cost to determine the price. Margin is the percentage of the final price that is profit. Using margins is more accurate for brokerage financial health.

faq.question: How can I track realized margins on a Mac?
faq.answer: You need a tool that connects your TMS and accounting software. Platforms like Querri or Descartes Aljex offer dashboards that pull data from both sources to show you the final profit after all costs are paid.
